title: Parrot: Efficient Serving of LLM-based Applications with Semantic Variable
technique: Semantic Variable abstraction exposing request dependencies/performance criteria; DAG-aware scheduling, objective deduction, prefix-sharing kernels

optimized_metrics.evidence: LLM-based applications are more concerned about the end-to-end experience, rather than the latency of individual requests.
The get operation supports annotation of performance criteria, showing the end-to-end performance requirement of an application, which can be end-to-end latency or throughput
the ideal scheduling strategy should maximize the throughput [of the map stage] ... while minimizing request latency during the reduce stage
we use the setting that an LLM engine can keep its generation latency under 40 ms/s for latency-sensitive requests
the primary goal of Parrot's scheduler is to meet the varied performance goals of LLM applications while optimizing GPU cluster utilization.

headline_claim.text: Parrot achieves up to 11.7x speedup or 12x higher throughput compared with the state-of-the-art solutions.

reported_metrics.where: Figs 11-14,17-18 (average E2E latency / JCT of applications)

metric_definitions.definition_quote: the latency per output token, i.e. TPOT (Time-per-output-token)
metric_definitions.notes: engine capacity threshold set so per-token latency stays under 40 ms

metric_definitions.definition_quote: normalized latency (measured as request latency per number of output tokens)
should minimize the end-to-end time it takes to receive the final summary, rather than the latency of individual requests
metric_definitions.notes: application-level, includes client network latency (emulated 200-300 ms per request) in baselines

slo_spec: no SLO attainment; latency-sensitive engine capacity bounded so token latency <40 ms/s (approx. under 6144 batched tokens)
load_regime: mix of per-app runs and request-rate sweeps (chat vs map-reduce mixed); not trace replay
tradeoff_acknowledged: latency vs throughput conflict: large batch sizes increase throughput but degrade latency; individual request latency may be sacrificed for application-level latency
workloads: chain/map-reduce summary, Bing Copilot, GPTs apps, MetaGPT multi-agent, ShareGPT chat
extractor_notes: Objective is application-level E2E latency or throughput per app, chosen via declared criteria; arguably dual (per-request objective deduced). Metrics are means; no tails.
